chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Like the first hadith, and it added in it, so Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah said: 'I am your ransom, so I do not have a wife.' He (the Imam) said: 'Do you not have concubines?' Or he said: 'Mothers of children.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You are not single (unmarried).'

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتُ أَوْلَادٍ: Mothers of children (concubines who have borne children)
key_terms.عَزَبٍ: Single/Unmarried (specifically referring to having no wife or concubines)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes being 'single' (azab) in Shia jurisprudence regarding marriage obligations?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the legal definition of 'azab' (single/unmarried) by distinguishing between formal marital status and actual sexual availability. He clarifies that a man with concubines (*ummat al-walad*) or children is not considered 'single' for the purpose of specific marital obligations, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on practical sexual capacity over mere contractual status. This distinction is crucial for understanding the conditions under which marriage becomes obligatory (*wajib*) or recommended (*mustahabb*) in Shia fiqh.
